subject: Exposure calibration by invoice window — MSA & Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah.thompson@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exposure calibration by invoice window — MSA & Order Form redlines

Sarah — attaching the latest redlines (draft_msa_redline_v3.docx + a short exposure matrix). Thanks for the productive call this morning. Two points we want to capture cleanly in the MSA/Order Form:

1) Cap basis (annualized vs total): We heard Acme prefers a cap tied to fees paid over the entire Term to date, but your Procurement team asked whether we can do an invoice-window approach (e.g., greater of 12 months' fees or Total Fees). For Redwood's internal risk models, predictable periodic calibration (annualized) helps us size reinsurance and reserve.

2) Multiple / floor: Customer asked for a flat multiple (e.g., 3x fees). We usually resist uncapped multipliers — our typical play is: cap = greater of (fees paid in the prior 12 months) and (total fees paid to date) up to a defined numeric floor for smaller deals.

Suggested path for negotiation (simple):
- For standard SaaS usage: cap = the greater of (fees paid in the prior 12 months) or (total fees paid under the Order Form), but not to exceed USD 3,000,000 for this engagement.
- For security/data breach or willful misconduct carveouts: maintain carveouts for indemnity but limit to specific remedies (we can discuss higher cap or waiver for IP indemnities).

Please review the attached exposure matrix (orderform_exposure_matrix.xlsx) — it maps a few billing profiles to what the cap looks like under various formulations. Our ask: if Acme can accept the "greater of prior 12 months or total fees, capped at $3M" formulation, we can close pricing and move to signature.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call if helpful.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Exposure calibration by invoice window — MSA & Order Form redlines

Jordan — thanks for the note and the attachments. We reviewed with procurement + outside counsel (Mike). A few items from Acme's side:

- Our preference is to keep the cap simple and tied to actual consideration paid under the Order Form (total fees) rather than a rolling 12-month construct — that avoids gaming around front-loaded invoicing.
- If Redwood insists on a 12-month lookback, Acme would push for the greater of (12 months' fees) or (Total Fees) without a separate numeric cap.
- Regarding multiples: 3x is reasonable to discuss, but Acme typically seeks a floor equal to at least 12 months' fees and a multiplier not to exceed 2x for services providers.
- Carveouts: Acme will insist that exclusions for consequential damages remain intact; however, for IP infringement and willful misconduct, we expect to preserve indemnity remedies with higher or uncapped exposure.

Attached is a tracked-redline (Sarah_redline_MSA_v2.docx) and a short memo from counsel. If Redwood can accept the "greater of 12 months or total fees" formulation without a hard ceiling, we can move to procurement approval faster. Otherwise Procurement will need approval from their risk committee.

Happy to discuss Thursday 8/10am PT.

— Sarah
Sarah Thompson
Sr. Counsel, Acme Corp
sarah.thompson@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exposure calibration by invoice window — MSA & Order Form redlines

Folks — quick legal read on Acme's position and recommended negotiating posture:

Summary of Acme asks:
- Cap tied to Total Fees or greater of Total/12-months, and potentially no numeric ceiling.
- Multipliers: Acme proposes <=2x; they want a floor of at least 12 months' fees.
- Carveouts: they will insist on uncapped IP indemnity and remedies for willful misconduct.

Our risk tolerance and options:
- Commercial compromise: agree to "greater of prior 12 months' fees or total fees paid under the Order Form" but include a negotiated numeric ceiling for this contract only (e.g., $3M) that scales with ARR for renewals. This preserves a predictable upper bound for loss exposure while giving Acme the billing-window logic they request.
- Multipliers: avoid open-ended multiples. If Acme insists on a multiple, we can offer a sliding multiple tied to annual committed spend (e.g., 1x for <$500k ARR, 2x for $500k–$2M, 3x for >$2M) but capped at the numeric ceiling.
- Carveouts: maintain standard carveouts for (i) IP infringement (handled via indemnity with explicit sub-limit), (ii) gross negligence/willful misconduct (no cap or higher cap), and (iii) statutory liabilities that cannot be excluded. For security/data incidents involving customer data, propose a separate protocol for incident response and a supplemental liability bucket (higher sub-cap) rather than a fully uncapped liability.

Ask: Jordan, can you propose the $3M ceiling to Acme as a one-time concession and offer the scaling multiple for renewal tiers? That keeps our exposure bounded while providing Acme with the substance they asked for. Also attach a one-page summary of tradeoffs for their Procurement team (redlines_summary.pdf).

— Laura Bennett
Director, Contract & Commercial Legal, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exposure calibration by invoice window — MSA & Order Form redlines

Sarah — appreciate the candid feedback and the redlines. After alignment with our legal team, here's a clean compromise we can put in the MSA/Order Form for Acme's review:

Proposed language (high level):
- Liability cap = the greater of (i) fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (ii) total fees actually paid under the Order Form to date, but in no event to exceed Three Million United States Dollars (USD 3,000,000) for the initial Term.
- Multipliers/floor: we will accept a floor concept but not an uncapped multiple; for this deal we will offer the effective floor described above and agree to a renewal-based sliding multiple (1x–3x) tied to committed spend for subsequent terms.
- Carveouts: preserve indemnity for IP infringement (sublimit of $5M), and no cap for claims arising from willful misconduct or criminal acts. Security/data incidents will have a separate incident sub-cap of $1M and standard remediation obligations.

If Acme is comfortable with the above (the numeric ceiling + the billing-window basis), we will:
1) Update the draft MSA redline and Order Form.
2) Send a one-page tradeoff summary to Procurement (attaching redlines_summary.pdf).
3) Confirm sign-off window for procurement (aiming for signature by end of July).

Next steps: Would Acme be willing to accept the proposed compromise? Happy to take a 15-min call Friday 9:30am PT to finalize.

Thanks — Jordan
